passages.title: Variable
passages.text: A variable is a named storage location in memory used to hold data that can change during program execution. It allows programs to store, update, and retrieve values dynamically.

passages.title: Data type
passages.text: A data type defines the kind of value a variable can hold, such as integer, string, or boolean. It determines how the data is stored and what operations can be performed on it.

passages.title: Constant
passages.text: A constant is a value that cannot be changed once it is assigned. It is used to store fixed values like mathematical constants or configuration settings.

passages.title: Operator
passages.text: An operator is a symbol that performs an operation on one or more values, such as addition, subtraction, or comparison. It is used to manipulate data within expressions.

passages.title: Expression
passages.text: An expression is a combination of variables, values, and operators that evaluates to a result. It is used to perform calculations or logical evaluations in a program.

passages.title: Control flow
passages.text: Control flow refers to the order in which instructions are executed in a program. It determines how decisions, loops, and sequences are handled during execution.

passages.title: Selection
passages.text: Selection is a control structure that allows a program to choose between different paths based on conditions. It is commonly implemented using if/else statements.

passages.title: Iteration
passages.text: Iteration is the repetition of a set of instructions until a condition is met. It is implemented using loops such as for and while loops.

passages.title: Algorithm
passages.text: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or completing a task. It must be finite, precise, and effective.

passages.title: Sequence
passages.text: Sequence refers to the order in which instructions are executed in a program. Each instruction runs one after another unless control flow changes it.

passages.title: Class
passages.text: A class is a blueprint for creating objects in object-oriented programming. It defines attributes and methods that describe the behaviour and properties of objects.

passages.title: Object
passages.text: An object is an instance of a class that contains real values and behaviour. It represents a specific entity in a program.

passages.title: Instance
passages.text: An instance is a specific occurrence of a class created in memory. Each instance has its own set of attribute values.

passages.title: Method
passages.text: A method is a function defined inside a class that describes behaviours of objects. It operates on object data and defines actions.

passages.title: Attribute
passages.text: An attribute is a variable stored inside a class that describes the properties of an object. It holds the state of an object.

passages.title: Encapsulation
passages.text: Encapsulation is the bundling of data and methods within a class while restricting direct access to internal data. It improves security and modularity.

passages.title: Inheritance
passages.text: Inheritance allows one class to acquire properties and methods from another class. It supports code reuse and hierarchical relationships.

passages.title: Polymorphism
passages.text: Polymorphism allows methods to take many forms depending on the object that is calling them. It enables flexibility in code behaviour.

passages.title: Abstraction
passages.text: Abstraction hides complex implementation details and shows only essential features. It simplifies program design and usage.

passages.title: Constructor
passages.text: A constructor is a special method used to initialise objects when they are created. It sets initial values for attributes.

passages.title: Sensor
passages.text: A sensor is a device that detects changes in the environment such as temperature, light, or motion. It converts physical data into electrical signals.

passages.title: Actuator
passages.text: An actuator is a component that converts electrical signals into physical movement or action. It is commonly used in robotics systems.

passages.title: Microcontroller
passages.text: A microcontroller is a small computer on a single chip used to control electronic devices. It processes inputs and controls outputs.

passages.title: Embedded system
passages.text: An embedded system is a computer system designed to perform a specific function within a larger device. It often operates in real-time.

passages.title: Signal processing
passages.text: Signal processing involves analysing and modifying signals from sensors. It is used to interpret real-world data in digital systems.

passages.title: Feedback loop
passages.text: A feedback loop is a system where outputs are fed back as inputs to control behaviour. It helps maintain stability and accuracy.

passages.title: PWM
passages.text: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) is a technique used to control power delivery by varying signal width. It is commonly used in motor control.

passages.title: GPIO
passages.text: General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO) pins allow microcontrollers to interface with external devices. They can be configured as input or output.

passages.title: Robotics control system
passages.text: A robotics control system manages the movement and behaviour of a robot. It processes sensor data and sends commands to actuators.

passages.title: Real-time system
passages.text: A real-time system processes data and responds within strict time constraints. It is critical in systems like robotics and automation.

passages.title: Authentication
passages.text: Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user or system. It ensures only authorised users can access resources.

passages.title: Authorisation
passages.text: Authorisation determines what an authenticated user is allowed to do. It controls access to system resources and actions.

passages.title: Encryption
passages.text: Encryption is the process of converting data into a coded format to prevent unauthorised access. It protects data during storage and transmission.

passages.title: Hashing
passages.text: Hashing converts data into a fixed-length value that cannot be easily reversed. It is commonly used for password storage.

passages.title: Firewall
passages.text: A firewall is a security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic. It helps block unauthorised access.

passages.title: Input validation
passages.text: Input validation ensures that data entered into a system is correct and safe. It helps prevent security vulnerabilities like injection attacks.

passages.title: Threat modelling
passages.text: Threat modelling is the process of identifying potential security threats in a system. It helps design safer software architectures.

passages.title: Least privilege principle
passages.text: The least privilege principle ensures users only have the minimum access required to perform their tasks. It reduces security risks.

passages.title: Vulnerability
passages.text: A vulnerability is a weakness in a system that can be exploited by attackers. It may lead to security breaches or data loss.

passages.title: Secure protocol
passages.text: A secure protocol is a set of rules for safe data communication over networks. It ensures confidentiality and integrity of data.

passages.title: HTML
passages.text: HTML is a markup language used to structure content on the web. It defines elements such as headings, paragraphs, and links.

passages.title: CSS
passages.text: CSS is used to style and format web pages. It controls layout, colours, fonts, and overall visual presentation.

passages.title: JavaScript
passages.text: JavaScript is a programming language used to add interactivity to web pages. It enables dynamic content and user interaction.

passages.title: Front-end
passages.text: Front-end refers to the part of a website that users interact with directly. It includes layout, design, and interface elements.

passages.title: Back-end
passages.text: Back-end refers to the server-side of a web application. It handles data processing, storage, and application logic.

passages.title: API
passages.text: An API is a set of rules that allows different software systems to communicate. It enables data exchange between applications.

passages.title: HTTP/HTTPS
passages.text: HTTP and HTTPS are protocols used for transferring data over the web. HTTPS provides secure encrypted communication.

passages.title: DOM
passages.text: The Document Object Model represents a web page as a structured tree. It allows scripts to dynamically access and modify content.

passages.title: Responsive design
passages.text: Responsive design ensures websites adapt to different screen sizes and devices. It improves usability across platforms.

passages.title: Web server
passages.text: A web server stores and delivers web content to users over the internet. It processes requests from browsers and sends responses.

passages.title: Script
passages.text: A script is a set of instructions written to automate tasks. It is often used to perform repetitive operations efficiently.

passages.title: Workflow
passages.text: A workflow is a sequence of automated or manual steps in a process. It helps organise and streamline tasks.

passages.title: Automation
passages.text: Automation is the use of technology to perform tasks with minimal human intervention. It increases efficiency and reduces errors.

passages.title: Scheduler
passages.text: A scheduler is a system that runs tasks at specified times or intervals. It is commonly used in operating systems and servers.

passages.title: CI/CD
passages.text: CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment. It automates software testing and deployment processes.

passages.title: Testing framework
passages.text: A testing framework is a set of tools used to automate software testing. It helps ensure code quality and reliability.

passages.title: Deployment pipeline
passages.text: A deployment pipeline automates the process of delivering software from development to production. It ensures consistent releases.

passages.title: Task runner
passages.text: A task runner automates repetitive development tasks such as minification or compilation. It improves workflow efficiency.

passages.title: Batch processing
passages.text: Batch processing executes a group of tasks without manual intervention. It is useful for handling large data sets efficiently.

passages.title: Bot
passages.text: A bot is an automated program that performs tasks over the internet or within software systems. It can simulate human actions.
